clue.text: Backward boy intended to show resistance

indicators.note: backward tells us to read the boy's name from right to left

parts.note: Ed is a common short boy's name
one's intended is the person one is engaged to marry, a fiancé

explanation.surface: A shy young man means to stand up for himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Defiance is open resistance to authority, so the two words are close synonyms.

clue.text: Artfully fingered international bomber during questioning

indicators.note: artfully suggests cunning rearrangement, so these letters are shuffled

parts.note: B- is a prefix for bomber aircraft, as in B-52

explanation.surface: A captured airman is skilfully interrogated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Artfully' rearranges FINGERED with I and B; 'during' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A debriefing is the questioning of someone, such as a pilot, after a mission.

clue.text: Firmly in favour of protecting upper-class fogey

indicators.note: protecting means holding something safely inside

parts.note: for means in favour of
a square is a conventional, old-fashioned person

explanation.surface: Someone stands solidly behind a posh old fuddy-duddy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'protecting' puts U inside FOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Foursquare used as an adverb means solidly and firmly, as in standing foursquare behind someone.

clue.text: Semi-diaphanous round, small bug

indicators.note: round suggests the letters are turned about into a new order
semi means half, so the back half of the word is dropped

explanation.surface: A tiny insect is half see-through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Semi-' leaves DIAPH, the first half of 'diaphanous', and 'round' rearranges those five letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An aphid is a tiny sap-sucking insect such as a greenfly, so a small bug.

clue.text: Cardinal's heartily against making profits

parts.note: cardinal and capital both mean principal or chief

indicators.note: heartily means take the heart, the middle letters, of the word

explanation.surface: A churchman speaks out strongly against making money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartily' takes GAINS, the heart of 'against'; 'making' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital gains are profits made from selling assets for more than they cost.

clue.text: I try to meet them in the same place

parts.note: a bid is an attempt or try
'em is the informal clipped form of them

explanation.surface: Someone hopes to meet a group at a shared venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to meet' simply joins the pieces. The answer is the Latin word used in footnotes to send the reader back to the source just cited.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin term, abbreviated ibid., literally means in the same place and is used in references.

clue.text: Work out a route for escape

parts.note: to break a code is to work it out
a way is a route

explanation.surface: Someone plots a path to freedom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A breakaway is an escape or separation from a group, as in a cycle race.

clue.text: Gets accommodation

definitions.meaning: dated slang: to dig something is to understand or appreciate it
dated British slang for lodgings, a rented room

explanation.definitionFit: Digs is old British slang for rented lodgings, and to dig is slang for grasp or understand.

clue.text: Amount he regularly gives mum

indicators.note: regularly means take every other letter

explanation.surface: A child gives his mother a sum of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of 'Amount he'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mum as an adjective means silent, as in keep mum, a synonym of speechless.

clue.text: Desperately spur Bush to make improvements

indicators.note: desperately suggests something done wildly and in disorder, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone urges a president to raise his game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desperately' rearranges the letters of SPUR and BUSH.
explanation.definitionFit: Brush-ups are quick revisions that polish skills, which makes them improvements.

clue.text: Handicap — or talent?

definitions.meaning: in horse racing a handicap is the extra load a horse must carry
a talent was an ancient unit of mass used for silver and gold

explanation.definitionFit: A racehorse's handicap is measured in pounds carried, and the ancient talent was a measure of heaviness.

clue.text: Allow daughter to be entertained by acrobat and terpsichorean

indicators.note: being entertained by someone is being taken in as a guest, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a balancer is an acrobat performing feats of balance
to let means to allow

explanation.surface: A girl is permitted to watch a circus act and a dancer.
explanation.walkthrough: Terpsichore was the Greek Muse of dance; 'and' is a link joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Terpsichorean means relating to dancing, after Terpsichore, the Muse of dance; used as a noun it is a dancer.

clue.text: Advantageous position within the regional bar

parts.note: within means in the interior of
in northern English dialect, especially Yorkshire, the is shortened to t'
a rack is a toothed bar that meshes with a pinion

explanation.surface: An insider has a good spot in the local pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' tempts as a pub, and 'regional' as a local one; in fact they give RACK and the dialect T' of northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the inside track is an idiom for holding a favourable position, from the shorter inner lane of a racecourse.

clue.text: Revealing dead princess's emotional resolution

parts.note: Diana, Princess of Wales, who died in 1997, is known as Di
closure is a sense of emotional resolution after a loss

explanation.surface: A tabloid story about a late princess finds peace.
explanation.walkthrough: Di is the popular name for Diana, Princess of Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Disclosure is the act of revealing, so the noun matches 'revealing' used as a verbal noun.

clue.text: Without energy, Helen talked about a bell ringing

indicators.note: about suggests the letters are moved around
without means the letter is left out of the name

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Helen, exhausted, gossips about a bell tolling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' drops one E from HELEN; 'about' rearranges the rest with TALKED.
explanation.definitionFit: A death knell is the tolling of a bell to announce a death.

clue.text: Sounds like one who tries embarrassingly hard to please animals

indicators.note: sounds like tells us the answer is a word said the same as the phrase that follows

parts.words: one who tries embarrassingly hard to please
parts.note: a fawner is a toady who flatters servilely

explanation.surface: A sycophant is compared to creatures by their noise.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent FAWNER, a flatterer, sounds the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Fauna is the collective term for the animal life of a region.

clue.text: Personal advantage in home, sadly, is with male

parts.note: in tennis 'ad' is short for advantage

indicators.note: sadly suggests things gone wrong, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man feels at home, sadly, enjoying his advantage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges IN and HOME into HOMINE; 'is with' joins M.
explanation.definitionFit: An argument made ad hominem is personal, attacking the opponent rather than the case.

clue.text: The boys who are completely blameless?

definitions.meaning: the folk song Green Grow the Rushes, O has the line 'two, two

explanation.walkthrough: Green Grow the Rushes, O is a traditional English counting song; its second verse is about the two boys.
explanation.definitionFit: Lily-white describes someone spotless and innocent, and the song's two boys bear that epithet.

clue.text: Region in Aragon or the Asturias?

indicators.note: in tells us the answer lies inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A geography question asks where an area of Spain lies.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pulls toward Spanish geography, and Aragon is indeed in Spain's north-east; but the answer is spelt out inside 'aragoN OR THE ASTurias'.
explanation.definitionFit: The north-east is a region of a country, such as England's, lying in that compass direction.

clue.text: Wrecked Chay Blyth's penultimate boat

indicators.note: wrecked suggests something broken up, so these letters are rearranged
penultimate means last but one, so we take the second-to-last letter of the name

explanation.surface: A famous yachtsman's vessel comes to grief.
explanation.walkthrough: Chay Blyth is a British yachtsman who sailed single-handed round the world, so the surface reads as his shipwreck; T is fourth of the five letters in his surname.
explanation.definitionFit: A yacht is a sailing or pleasure boat.

clue.text: Lament disastrous mass failure of memory

indicators.note: disastrous suggests ruin and disorder, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a block is a solid mass of material

explanation.surface: Someone mourns a widespread forgetting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disastrous' rearranges LAMENT into MENTAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A mental block is an inability to recall something, a temporary lapse of memory.

clue.text: Like Porgy and Bess at first are abused by many

indicators.note: at first means take the opening letter
abused suggests ill-treatment, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, hence many

explanation.surface: The lovers of Gershwin's opera are mistreated by a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porgy and Bess' looks like Gershwin's opera, but a porgy is a fish; 'abused' rearranges ARE.
explanation.definitionFit: Porgies are sea fish of the same family, so this fish is one like a porgy.

clue.text: Work involves removing heads from seafood

indicators.note: removing heads means cutting off the front letters of the word

parts.note: octopus is eaten as seafood

explanation.surface: A chef's job means beheading the catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removing heads from' cuts OCT from the front of OCTOPUS, perhaps one 'head' for each letter; 'involves' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An opus is a work, especially a numbered musical composition.

clue.text: In which I find a means to play music

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the following words

explanation.surface: Someone describes the stereo they use.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'whicH I FInd'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hi-fi is high-fidelity sound equipment for playing recorded music.

clue.text: Heads of publicly listed industries all need to be flexible

indicators.note: heads of means take the first letter of each word that follows

explanation.surface: Advice that quoted companies must adapt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heads of' takes the initial letter of each word from 'publicly' to 'to'; 'be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Pliant means bending easily, which is a synonym of flexible.

clue.text: Plan to work on Shed clue

indicators.note: to work on something is to rework it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A garden-shed puzzle is to be tackled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work on' rearranges the letters of SHED and CLUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A schedule is a timetable, which is a plan of when things will happen.

clue.text: Ultimately, "Scarlet Letter" is about disgrace

indicators.note: is about says the letter goes round the other piece

parts.note: sigma is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: ultimately means finally, so we take the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Hawthorne's novel The Scarlet Letter is a tale of public shame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ultimately' takes T, the end of 'Scarlet'; 'is about' puts SIGMA around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A stigma is a mark of shame, so it means disgrace; Hester Prynne's scarlet A was one.

clue.text: Enemy of King Charles has no master, clearly

parts.note: CR stands for Carolus Rex, Latin for King Charles
O is nought, zero, so nothing
M is an abbreviation for master, as in MA
well can mean clearly, as in 'see well'

explanation.surface: A foe of the king is plainly his own man.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's full 'Enemy of King Charles' points at Oliver Cromwell, who led Parliament against Charles I, while 'King Charles' also gives CR.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver Cromwell led Parliament's armies against Charles I, making him the king's chief enemy.
